blocking_findings.finding: Bypass validation used a nonexistent normalized field and defaulted absence to empty.
blocking_findings.remediation: Raw pull-request review protection is now required; bypass allowances must be present and all users, teams, and apps empty. Missing data fails. Personal-repository dismissal capability is explicitly modeled and nonempty actors fail.

blocking_findings.finding: The validator accepted a hand-built normalized document and did not fetch GitHub.
blocking_findings.remediation: The provider tool now fetches bounded raw endpoints, preserves a content-hashed raw envelope, validates endpoint provenance, normalizes real provider wrappers, and rejects manual normalized input as evidence.

blocking_findings.finding: One required approval was operationally impossible with only the author identity verified.
blocking_findings.remediation: The reviewer registry is truthfully empty, provider application is explicitly blocked, and provider validation requires a non-owner qualifying collaborator before application.

blocking_findings.finding: The required check used a context string without an App binding.
blocking_findings.remediation: The payload now uses checks with GitHub Actions App ID 15368, and raw check-run App identity must be read back on an exact-head test PR before application.

blocking_findings.finding: The candidate defined the workflow and tests that claimed to gate itself.
blocking_findings.remediation: Candidate proof and trusted gate are separated. Default-branch trusted code never executes PR source and posts an app-bound custom check directly to the exact head after validating workflow identity and exact-head review evidence.

blocking_findings.finding: Current main contains write-capable recovery workflows inconsistent with the claimed posture.
blocking_findings.remediation: Exact workflows and blobs are inventoried as a blocking active-lane dependency. Worker 3 does not edit PR #53-owned paths; provider application cannot proceed until reviewed remediation lands and this branch is rebased.

non_blocking_findings.remediation: Both governance modules now have explicit entry-point guards and are import-testable.
Provider validation now covers lock_branch, allow_fork_syncing, block_creations, restrictions, CODEOWNER review setting, and bypass actors.
Live cross-lane heads are no longer embedded as current claims in policy documentation; timestamped evidence remains historical.
Dependency audit remains visible but is no longer part of the deterministic required aggregate.

remaining_gates: fresh independent review of the remediated head

additional_internal_findings.finding: A trusted workflow triggered by review or workflow-run events cannot assume github.sha is the default-branch commit.
additional_internal_findings.remediation: The workflow now resolves the repository default branch at run start, records the exact checked-out SHA, and fails if that SHA equals the candidate head.

additional_internal_findings.finding: The first provider-capture design incorrectly required the harmless test-PR head to equal the current main SHA.
additional_internal_findings.remediation: Current main and the test-PR check head are normalized and validated independently; regression coverage proves they may differ.

additional_internal_findings.finding: Reviewer capacity alone did not prove the source-controlled reviewer registry matched a qualifying provider identity.
additional_internal_findings.remediation: Provider validation now requires an open, timestamped registry and exact membership in GitHub’s qualifying non-owner collaborator set.
